full_text:
In a wealthy merchant’s house in Vijayanagara, a skinny and agile cat-burglar named Somu climbed down the wide kitchen chimney flue at midnight to rob the brass and silverware.
However, during the previous day, the kitchen masons had narrowed the lower hearth with new bricks to improve the draft!
Halfway down the chimney, Somu got wedged tightly between the soot-covered bricks!
He could not move forward, nor could he pull himself back up to the roof!
He was trapped like an iron cork in a bottle!

Hearing muffled groans and soot dropping into the empty fireplace, the terrified merchant ran to Tenali Raman’s house next door, shouting that a demon was dwelling in his chimney!

Tenali arrived carrying no weapons or ladders.
He peered into the fireplace and saw two human legs dangling three feet above the hearth grate, kicking frantically.

Tenali smiled: 'Merchant, do not call the soldiers with sledgehammers; they will ruin your expensive chimney.
Let us prepare a midnight meal to welcome our guest!'

Tenali instructed the servants to bring a small bundle of dry chili peppers, a handful of bitter sulfur powder, and a bundle of damp green coconut husks.
Tenali placed the materials on the hearth grate directly beneath the dangling feet, and lit a small, smoldering fire.
Thick, pungent, white acrid smoke—infused with concentrated red chili fumes—began billowing up the chimney shaft!

Within five seconds, a frantic, coughing, tearful screaming exploded from inside the chimney:
*‘COUGH! ACHO0! MERCY! I AM NOT A DEMON!
I AM SOMU THE BURGLAR! I AM SUFFOCATING!
PULL ME DOWN! CALL THE POLICE! DO ANYTHING, BUT PUT OUT THE CHILIES!’*

Tenali poured a cup of water onto the fire, and called up:
'Somu, if we pull your legs down, will you confess all your burglaries to the magistrate?'
'YES! YES! I SWEAR UPON MY MOTHER’S HEAD!' shrieked the weeping thief.

Tenali and the servants gripped the dangling feet, gave a coordinated heave, and pulled Somu down through the brick opening!
Somu tumbled onto the hearth floor, completely black with soot from head to toe, coughing, sneezing, tears streaming down his face, looking like a chimney demon!

The guards arrived and took the thief into custody.
Somu led them to his hideout, where thirty stolen silver platters were recovered.
The merchant thanked Tenali with a basket of sweets, laughing at how easily a handful of dried chilies and a bit of smoke can disarm the craftiest housebreaker.
moral: A trapped burglar cannot escape the smoke of his own crime; patience outwaits violence. [PT]
